title: Human Factors practice set 2
src: Bali AR, Additional Practice Questions: Human Factors

qs.q: Pilots are more easily inclined to make mistakes when:
o: They are not constrained by time.
They are not able to assess and control the risks involved in a situation.

qs.q: Low levels of arousal are:
The amount of light which strikes the retina is controlled by:
Which of the following statements in regard to motivation is correct?
o: Too much motivation may result in hypo vigilance and thus in a decrease in attention.
Motivation will reduce the task automation process hence performance will degrade.
The learning process is vastly improved with motivation.

qs.q: Five hours after a rapid decompression at FL 320 you experience pain in the joints. Which of following answers is correct?
o: This symptom indicates decompression sickness and will disappear with in 24 hours.
This phenomenon is treated by breathing 100% oxygen under pressure.
You should ask for medical advice since this is a symptom of decompression sickness.

qs.q: A high degree of cockpit automation may alter the traditional tasks of the pilots in a way, that:
o: The crew always maintains situational awareness by being more alert.
The crew pays more attention to be always in loop.
The attention of the cockpit crew will become reduced with the consequence of being out of the loop'.

qs.q: Long-term memory is an essential component of the pilot's knowledge and expertise.
o: The information stored in long-term memory is always fresh and easy to retrieve.
It is desirable to pre-activate knowledge stored in long-term memory to have it available when required.
The capacity of long-term memory is limited to a few weeks.

qs.q: The human information processing system is highly efficient compared to computers because of its:
What are easily observable indications of stress?
o: Rising of the blood pressure, pupils narrowing, stabbing pain around the heart.
Perspiration, flushed skin, dilated pupils,fast breathing.
Faster, deep inhalation, stabbing pain around the heart.

qs.q: CRM (Crew Resource Management) training is:
o: Intended to develope effectiveness of crew performance by improving attitudes towards flight safety and human relationship management.
Not intended to change the individual's attitude towards other crew members.
Intended to alter an individual's stress management capabilities.

qs.q: As a result of automation in cockpits:
o: Coordination between the members is facilitated by the provision of more precise and more important information.
Communication and coordination call for an even greater effort on the part of the crew members.
Man-man communication has been significantly improved.

qs.q: Which statement is correct?
o: Oxygen diffusion from the lungs into the blood does not depend on partial oxygen pressure.
Oxygen diffusion from the blood into the cells depends on the partial oxygen pressure gradient.
The diffusion gradient is higher at altitude than at sea level.

qs.q: A pilot after pulling out of a steep dive, moves the control column instinctively and firmly forward may suffer a:
A pilot has flown an aircraft as a Captain for 1000 hrs.With what phase of motor programme he can be associated with?
Too low a workload can:
Thinking on human reliability is changing.
o: Human errors can be avoided. All it takes is to be vigilant and to extend one's knowledge.
It is thought that it will be possible to eliminate errors in the near future.
Human errors are now considered as being inherent to the cognitive function of human and are generally inescapable.

qs.q: Gases of physiological importance to man are:
You can survive at any altitude, provided that;
o: Enough oxygen, pressure and heat is available.
21% oxygen is available in the air you breath in.
Pressure respiration is guaranteed for that altitude.

qs.q: Fatigue and permanent concentration:
o: Do not affect hypoxia at all.

qs.q: An increase in the amount of carbon dioxide in the blood leads to:
o: A decrease of acidity in the blood.
A reduction of red blood cells.

qs.q: The total pressure of a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of the gases which compose the mixture corresponds to:
The barometric pressure has dropped to 1/2 of the pressure at sea level at:
Boyle's law is directly applicable in case of: The expansion of trapped gasses in the human body with increasing altitude.
o: The expansion of trapped gases in the body with increasing altitude.

qs.q: Dalton's law explains the occurrence of :
ADDITIONAL PRACTICE QUESTIONS: HUMAN FACTORS 26. The respiratory process consists mainly of:
o: The diffusion of oxygen through the respiratory membranes into the blood, transportation to the cells, diffusion into the cells and elimination of carbon dioxide from the body.
The transportation of oxygen to the cell and the elimination of carbon monoxide.
The transportation of oxygen to the cell and the elimination of nitrogen.

qs.q: Carbon monoxide poisoning;
o: Is more likely to occur in aeroplanes where the cabin heat is technically supplied by coating the exhaust.
Is more likely to occur in aeroplanes with twin-engines because of high engine efficiency.

qs.q: In the following list you will find several symptoms listed for hypoxia and carbon monoxide poisoning. Please mark those referring to carbon monoxide poisoning.
o: Muscular spasms, mental confusion, impairment of hearing.
High levels of arousal, increased error proneness, lack of accuracy.
